answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-bonded vouching: a new agent starts as an isolated island with near-zero trust and must earn attestations from established peers before it can transact at full volume. Each peer that vouches locks a deposit that thaws as slowly as a glacier, so creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits for months, a cost that scales linearly with the attack. A trusted hub acts as an oasis, lending its reputation only to agents it has verified, and if a vouched agent cheats, the hub's own deposit is slashed, so vouching stays honest.
